about.text: Mongolian dried curd, a long-standing portable food of herding families. Most is made from the yoghurt of cows or yaks, although any livestock milk or yoghurt can be used. The curd is spread on the sloping roof of the ger to dry in the sun, then shaped. Sugar is sometimes added. Once hard, it keeps for a long time.

how.text: Mongolian aaruul is the curd of soured or yoghurt-fermented milk, drained in cloth, pressed, cut and dried in sun and air on the yurt roof. It becomes a hard snack that keeps through winter.
